correctness.rationale: For all n≥2 every pair of graph vertices is an exact resolving neighborhood: {u1,u2} via apices, {u_a,v_i} via spoke vertex–edge pair, and {v_i,v_j} via corresponding spoke edges. Singleton neighborhoods arise only from incident vertex–edge pairs; n=2 forces all 4, n=3 forces u1,u2,v1,v3, n≥4 forces v1,vn. Remaining neighborhoods contain ≥2 vertices and are implied by the pair inequalities. For n≥4 the n free vertices form fractional vertex cover of K_n; summing all pair constraints yields weight at least n/2, tight exactly when all free weights equal 1/2 (n≥3). Endpoint weights contribute 2: λ=(n+4)/2. The n=2,3 exceptions follow. Independently reconstructed all original mixed-distance neighborhoods and solved indicator and original absolute-difference LP for n=2,...,10 using SciPy HiGHS, obtaining predicted optima and same vectors; finite replay corroborates, arbitrary n follows the proof.
residual_risks: Explicit λ_M is the indicator resolving-cover relaxation; the published binary optimization coefficients are not generally equivalent after LP relaxation.
